question:
(a) State the relation between resistivity and temperature for a conductor over a small temperature range.
(b) The resistivity of a metal at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is $1.6\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\text{m}$. If $\alpha=4.0\times10^{-3}\,\text{K}^{-1}$, calculate its resistivity at $100^\circ\text{C}$.
(c) Why is the relation valid only over a limited temperature range?

options.A:
(a) $\rho_T=\rho_0[1-\alpha(T-T_0)]$.
(b) $\rho_{100}=0.96\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\text{m}$.
(c) The relation is exact for all temperatures.
options.B:
(a) $\rho_T=\rho_0+\alpha(T-T_0)$.
(b) $\rho_{100}=4.016\times10^{-3}\,\Omega\,\text{m}$.
(c) It is valid only when temperature is zero.
options.C:
(a) $\rho_T=\rho_0[1+\alpha(T+T_0)]$.
(b) $\rho_{100}=2.56\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\text{m}$.
(c) It fails because resistance is independent of temperature.
options.D:
(a) Over a small range, $\rho_T=\rho_0[1+\alpha(T-T_0)]$.
(b) $\rho_{100}=(1.6\times10^{-8})[1+(4.0\times10^{-3})(100)]=2.24\times10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\text{m}$.
(c) This is an approximate linear relation and may not remain linear over a large temperature range.
